sentence: This project studies how the brain changes with the menopause and how hormones, cardiovascular health, and menopausal symptoms affect those changes.
This project tests whether a cardiokine protects against diabetic cardiomyopathy in diabetic mouse models and studies how it works in cardiomyocytes.
This project studies how a bacteriophage kills Pseudomonas aeruginosa and protects its genome from nucleases inside a lipid vesicle.
This project studies how podocytes keep their shape and adhesion in the glomerulus by examining the components and dynamics of their cytoskeleton.
This project studies why T cell development declines with age, using a mutant mouse model and an Artificial Thymic Organoid system.
This project studies the cellular ecology of Barrett’s esophagus tissue in patients who later developed esophageal cancer and in patients who did not.
This project studies how meningeal lymphatics help the zebrafish nervous system regenerate by regulating the immune response and cerebral spinal fluid.
This project tries to find out how to reverse senescence and immune suppression in T cells that target tumors in head and neck cancer.
This project analyzes genomic, transcriptomic and metabolomic data to find biomarkers of cisplatin resistance and ways to prevent it.
This project uses deep learning on brain data to find signatures that predict which patients with major depressive disorder respond to repetitive transcranial magnetic stimulation.
This project creates mice that cannot form thyroxine in thyroglobulin, to learn how thyroxine affects development, growth, behavior, hearing, and body weight.
This project tries to find the key mechanisms and molecular targets that stop tumor progression in rhabdomyosarcoma.
This project studies how trophoblast cell lineage develops and works, since defects in it can cause early pregnancy loss.
This project builds a natural language processing tool that gives therapists feedback to improve culturally responsive care.
This project builds a platform that combines data from unobtrusive sensors to predict anxiety and memory states continuously.
This project builds a brain-computer interface that turns brain activity into intended words for people who lost the ability to speak.
This project builds controlled release technology to slowly deliver HIV vaccines and studies what makes vaccine-induced immunity last.
This project builds imaging technology that combines computer vision, light-sheet microscopy, and imaging probes to study cellular signals.
This project builds high throughput omics-based assays to find molecular signatures that predict when acute pain turns into chronic pain.
This project builds a method that combines optical and DNA barcodes to track changes in single cells over time and read their omics data.
